content.en: Machine learning algorithms are being used to predict the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in various medical scenarios. These algorithms, such as support vector machines, random forest, and logistic regression, are being employed to develop risk prediction models for cancer patients, COVID-19 patients, critically ill patients, and those undergoing surgery. By analyzing different predictors and using optimization techniques, these algorithms aim to outperform existing scoring systems and improve the accuracy of VTE risk prediction.
content.da: Maskinlæringsalgoritmer anvendes til at forudsige risikoen for venøs tromboembolisme (VTE) i forskellige medicinske scenarier. Disse algoritmer, såsom support vector machines, random forest og logistic regression, anvendes til at udvikle risikoprediktionsmodeller for kræftpatienter, COVID-19 patienter, kritisk syge patienter og personer, der gennemgår operation. Ved at analysere forskellige prediktorer og anvende optimeringsteknikker har disse algoritmer til formål at overgå eksisterende scoringssystemer og forbedre nøjagtigheden af VTE risikoprediktion.

critic.en: Oh, boy... Do we really need yet another "innovation" that replaces expert judgment with a black box algorithm? The idea of using machine learning to predict VTE risk might sound appealing at first glance, but it comes with a host of ethical and practical issues. Are these algorithms replicating or merely replacing human judgment? What happens when the prediction model is so complex that even its developers cannot fully explain it? And, most importantly, are we prepared to accept the consequences of basing life-or-death decisions on a system that could potentially carry bias?
critic.da: Så er det altså maskinlæringsalgoritmer, der skal afgøre, om vi skal frygte blodpropper? Jeg kan ikke bare følge med påstander om, at maskinerne er vores nye livliner. Hvorfor tror du, at algoritmebaserede løsninger kan forbedre patientplejen, i stedet for at skabe nye lag af usikkerhed?

potential.en: There are many ways technology is helping to predict VTE risk! It's truly amazing to see how machine learning algorithms can be utilized in the medical field. By combining various predictors and using optimization techniques, these algorithms have the potential to greatly improve the accuracy of VTE risk assessment for a wide range of patients. I'm excited to see further developments in this area and the positive impact it will have on patient care!
potential.da: Brugere af maskinlæringsalgoritmer til at forudsige risikoen for VTE i sundhedssektoren viser, hvordan teknologien kan forbedre behandlingerne. Forudsigelsesmodellerne kan hjælpe med at beskytte sårbare patienter og sikre, at de får den rette opmærksomhed. Det er en lovende anvendelse af maskinlæring, der potentielt set har stor indflydelse.
